content:
{
  "claim": "recover_json_object does not apply last-wins duplicate-key recovery to fenced candidates, so a scoreable fenced object with repeated keys can be skipped and a later top-level object outside the fence returned instead.",
  "expected": "For content containing a fenced JSON object with repeated keys followed by a top-level object outside the fence, recover_json_object should return the fenced object with the last value for the repeated key, e.g. {\"a\": 2}.",
  "observed": "It returns the later top-level object, e.g. {\"b\": 3}, because the fenced pool only attempts strict parsing and skips duplicate-key recovery, then the top-level pool considers the later object first.",
  "reproducer": "```json\n{\"a\": 1, \"a\": 2}\n```\n{\"b\": 3}",
  "source_basis": "The documented rule says: \"A candidate that parses as strict JSON, or as JSON with repeated keys resolved last-wins, is scoreable\" and \"The object scored is the last one inside a code fence when any fence holds one, else the last top-level object in the text.\"",
  "execution_evidence": "none: no executable oracle",
  "scope": "Inputs with a fenced JSON object containing duplicate keys followed by a later top-level JSON object outside the fence.",
  "uncertainty": "None beyond the documented rule; the code's fenced branch explicitly skips _loads_last_wins."
}
